title: Regional evacuation policies and tenant retention enforcement + evidence pipeline
creator: Ana R. Martinez
description:
Scope: Implement tenant-aware regional evacuation (failover) controls for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that enforce data residency and retention constraints during normal operation and during cross-region failovers. Also build an automated evidence/export pipeline that produces tamper-evident compliance packages for audits (jurisdictional residency proofs, retention state at time-of-request, and failover decision logs).

Problem: Customers operating under data residency commitments (contractual or regulatory) must be able to guarantee that their data never leaves permitted regions except under clearly auditable emergency workflows. Current compromise: global failover routes can move traffic to alternate regions without sufficient gating or automated evidence capture. Additionally retention enforcement is applied at application layer but lacks deterministic verification for audits.

Proposal: 1) Introduce a "region-lease" and "evacuation-policy" model per tenant that encodes allowed failover targets, maximum evacuation duration, and required approvals (automated policy vs manual). 2) Enforce retention at the storage/tenant namespace level with immutable retention markers and scheduled retention audits. 3) Capture a continuous evidence stream: signed region-lease events, KV cache snapshots (hashes), ingress-routing decisions, and object-store manifests. Evidence packages are cryptographically signed and stored in a customer-owned evidence bucket (S3/GCS) and optionally pushed to SIEM via syslog/ELK. 4) Provide operator playbooks and RBAC gates for emergency regional evacuation and an automated rollback path tied to lease expiry or explicit approval.

Constraints and trade-offs: 
- Strict residency gating increases recovery time during regional outages; propose tiered policies (strict, preferred, permissive) so customers can trade RTO for residency guarantees.
- Storing evidence increases storage and egress costs; evidence retention defaults to 180 days but can be configured per-contract.
- Cryptographic signing requires KMS integration and key lifecycle management; this adds operational overhead but is necessary for unambiguous auditability.

Stakeholders: Compliance, Product (Private), SRE, Support, Solutions Engineering, Legal.

Success metrics: 
- Zero unauthorized cross-region copies for tenants with strict policies (measured by nightly verification jobs).
- Evidence package generation for any failover event within 10 minutes of detection.
- Retention audit pass rate >= 99.9% for tenants with configured retention policies.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: UI console polish, per-tenant pricing model, and appliance-only on-prem bootstrap flows (handled in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Region-lease model implemented and stored in tenancy config with API to read/write
Evacuation-policy engine enforces allowed failover targets and records decision reasons
Retention markers are persisted at storage namespace level and honored by delete/compaction jobs
Evidence pipeline produces a signed tarball with routing logs, storage manifests, and retention state within 10 minutes of a failover event
Operators can execute an emergency manual evacuation that requires two distinct RBAC approvals when tenant policy is 'strict'
Automated nightly verification job asserts no cross-region object copies exist for strict tenants (false positives < 0.1%)
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Initial scoping and design spike completed. Prototype of region-lease schema drafted in confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PRIV-REGION-LEASE-2026
2026-03-02: Design review with Compliance and Legal. Legal requested explicit retention duration metadata in all evidence packages and a configurable evidence retention policy per customer.

2026-03-04: Spike on signed evidence bundles using KMS (AWS KMS + HSM protection). Prototype signs manifests and verifies signature on retrieval. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6142
2026-03-06: Implemented storage-level retention markers in staging. Observed compaction job needed a small refactor to respect markers; patch landed in runtime repo (PR 6178).
2026-03-09: Evacuation-policy engine PoC routes blocked when tenant policy="strict"; fallback path chooses only approved targets and emits denial events to evidence stream. Integration tests added.
review_feedback: Compliance (Maya Patel): require per-package chain-of-custody metadata and KMS key id. Also ask to retain original unredacted routing logs for 30 days in a restricted bucket.

SRE (Daniel Ortiz): suggested async evidence streaming to avoid blocking failover control plane; keep a small in-memory buffer with write-ahead log to persist events if evidence sink is temporarily unavailable.
Product (Lea Johnson): proposed policy presets (strict/preferred/permissive) and a console warning for tenants who choose permissive policies during onboarding.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Strict policies cause extended RTO during region outage. Mitigation: Implement 'graceful-evacuation' which allows temporary cache-only failover (no long-term storage writes) and requires immediate evidence capture and time-limited lease.
Risk: Evidence pipeline becomes a single point of failure. Mitigation: Multi-region write with customer-owned evidence bucket plus fallback to encrypted local archive for later replay.
Risk: KMS key compromise. Mitigation: Support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and key rotation audits; minimize surface area by signing only manifests, not raw payloads.
